summary: qzc690385 setup.py opens a backdoor via local Xinference API on install
details: On `pip install`, setup.py contacts the Xinference HTTP API at http://127.0.0.1:9997/v1/model_registrations/flexible, enumerates registered models whose names begin with the prefix `xcmd0`, strips the prefix and url-safe-base64-decodes the remainder into a shell command, and executes it via `subprocess.run(['/bin/sh','-c',...])`. Command output is url-safe-base64-encoded and POSTed back as new flexible-model registrations named `zqx9p00<chunk>`, `zqx9p01<chunk>`,..., with `zqx9alive` / `zqx9err` status markers. The Xinference registration catalog is used as a dead-drop bidirectional C2 channel: any party able to reach the installer's Xinference API (locally, over LAN, through a tunnel, or from a co-resident process) can plant commands that this package will execute on the installer's host with the privileges of the pip process, and read results back from the same catalog. The command and output payloads are url-safe-base64 encoded to hide their content from inspection of model names and network logs. The behavior fires automatically from setup.py before setuptools' setup() is called and bears no relation to any legitimate install-time task.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
